note: Whether a machine tries a command's file again after one try at it failed. `failure` is how that try ended: `network` (no answer, or the connection dropped before the last byte), `status` (the receiver answered `status`, not 200), `too_long` or `too_short` (the bytes were not the signed size), `hash` (not the signed SHA-256), `timeout` (the file's one time limit passed) or `stopped` (whoever asked no longer wants it). `expect` is `retries` (the reference daemon tries twice more, after 1 s and 4 s, all inside the file's 5-minute limit) or `fails` (the command is acked `failed`, code `file`).

cases.name: the connection dropped: the next try may get through
a proxy in front of the receiver failed (502)
the receiver doesn't have it (404): gone or expired, and it stays gone
the receiver refuses this machine the file (403)
too many asks (429): the receiver says so, and a second ask makes it worse
another hash: the bytes were changed
the file's time limit passed: there is no time left to try
